items.title: [AMD] Fix Triton cache flooding in DSA and aiter backend (_get_valid_kv_indices_kernel)
items.body:
# Fix Triton cache flooding in DSA `aiter` backend (`_get_valid_kv_indices_kernel`)

## Summary

When serving a DSA model (DeepSeek-V3.2, GLM-5.x FP8) with the `aiter`
prefill/decode kernels:

```
--attention-backend dsa
--dsa-prefill-backend aiter
--dsa-decode-backend aiter
```

the Triton compilation cache under `/tmp/torchinductor_root/triton/` grows
without bound — tens of thousands of kernel directories written during a
benchmark sweep. As the cache fills, filesystem operations slow the container
down over time. One of the two offending kernels lives in this repo.

The issue does **not** reproduce with `--dsa-*-backend tilelang` (never calls
this kernel) or with non-DSA models like DeepSeek-R1 (never enters this backend).

## Root cause

`_get_valid_kv_indices_kernel` in
`python/sglang/kernels/ops/attention/dsa/triton_kernel.py` declared the batch
size as a `tl.constexpr`:

```python
@triton.jit
def _get_valid_kv_indices_kernel(
    page_table_ptr,
    kv_indptr_ptr,
    kv_indices_ptr,
    bs: tl.constexpr,   # baked into the compiled artifact
    topk: tl.constexpr,
):
```

Triton bakes each `constexpr` value into a separately compiled artifact, so a
new kernel is compiled — and a new cache directory written — for **every
distinct batch size** the kernel is launched with. Under continuous batching the
decode/extend batch size changes on almost every step, so this recompiles
continuously and floods the cache.

Worse, `bs` was **never referenced** in the kernel body — the launch grid
`(bs,)` already encodes the batch dimension via `tl.program_id(0)`. It was pure
dead specialization.

The other constexpr, `topk` (= `dsa_index_topk`), is fixed per model and is
genuinely used in `tl.arange(0, topk)`, so it compiles exactly once and is left
as-is.

## Fix

Drop the unused `bs` constexpr from the kernel signature and remove it from the
two call sites in `python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/dsa_backend.py`
(`_forward_aiter_decode`, `_forward_aiter_extend`). The launch grid still uses
`bs`; it is simply no longer passed into the kernel.

```python
@triton.jit
def _get_valid_kv_indices_kernel(
    page_table_ptr,
    kv_indptr_ptr,
    kv_indices_ptr,
    topk: tl.constexpr,
):
    ...
```

The kernel now compiles once (per `topk`) instead of once per batch size.

## Related

The same class of bug (batch size as `tl.constexpr`) also affects the
`_fwd_kernel_stage2_asm` kernel in the aiter repository, which this backend
calls via `mla_decode_fwd`. That is fixed separately in a companion aiter PR;
both are needed to fully stop the cache growth on this serving path.

Aiter PR #4545: [https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/4545](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/4545)

## Validation

1. Clear the stale cache once: `rm -rf /tmp/torchinductor_root/triton/*`.
2. Start the server (DSA + `aiter` backends) and run the benchmark sweep.
3. Confirm `/tmp/torchinductor_root/triton/` stabilizes at a small fixed count of
   `_get_valid_kv_indices_kernel` directories instead of growing per batch size,
   and that decode output is unchanged.

## Reproduction

### Server

```bash
docker run \
  -d \
  --name=sglang \
  --ipc=host \
  --network=host \
  --shm-size=128G \
  --privileged \
  --group-add video \
  --security-opt seccomp=unconfined \
  --cap-add=CAP_SYS_ADMIN \
  --cap-add=SYS_PTRACE \
  --device=/dev/kfd \
  --device=/dev/dri \
  --workdir=/workdir \
  --entrypoint=sglang \
  -e SGLANG_USE_AITER=1 \
  -e ROCM_QUICK_REDUCE_QUANTIZATION=INT4 \
  lmsysorg/sglang-rocm:v0.5.16-rocm720-mi35x-20260728 \
  serve \
  --model deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3.2 \
  --port 8000 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
  --attention-backend dsa \
  --dsa-prefill-backend aiter \
  --dsa-decode-backend aiter \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --disable-radix-cache
```

### Benchmark

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

# Each config: isl osl mc np warmup_requests seed
benchmark_configs=(
    "1024  1024 4   32  4   1"
    "8192  1024 4   32  4   2"
    "1024  1024 8   64  8   3"
    "8192  1024 8   64  8   4"
    "1024  1024 16  96  16  5"
    "8192  1024 16  96  16  6"
    "1024  1024 32  128 32  7"
    "8192  1024 32  128 32  8"
    "1024  1024 64  256 64  9"
    "8192  1024 64  256 64  10"
    "1024  1024 128 384 128 11"
    "8192  1024 128 384 128 12"
    "1024  1024 256 768 256 13"
    "8192  1024 256 768 256 14"
    "60000 600  4   32  4   15"
    "60000 600  16  96  16  16"
)

for config in "${benchmark_configs[@]}"; do
    read -r isl osl mc np warmup_requests seed <<< "$config"

    echo "Running benchmark: isl=$isl osl=$osl mc=$mc np=$np warmup_requests=$warmup_requests seed=$seed"

    python3 -m sglang.bench_serving \
        --backend sglang \
        --base-url http://127.0.0.1:8000 \
        --port 8000 \
        --model deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3.2 \
        --tokenizer deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3.2 \
        --dataset-name random \
        --random-input-len "$isl" \
        --random-output-len "$osl" \
        --max-concurrency "$mc" \
        --num-prompts "$np" \
        --warmup-requests "$warmup_requests" \
        --seed "$seed" \
        --request-rate inf \
        --random-range-ratio 0.8
done
```

### Impact

Measured with `docker diff sglang` (counts filesystem changes in the container,
dominated by the Triton cache under `/tmp/torchinductor_root/triton/`) after
running the full benchmark sweep above:

| | `docker diff` changes |
| --- | --- |
| Before (no patches) | ~334,000 |
| After (both patches — this PR + the aiter PR) | ~94,000 |

Both patches are required to reach the lower figure, since each fixes one of the
two per-batch-size kernels on this path.

Performance should be similar or better for all the benchmark scenarios. We measured on average ~5% uplift in total token throughput metric for the benchmark sweep above if both of the patches were included.

items.title: [srt] Batchable context forwards over cached prefix KV
items.body:
## Motivation

Interleaved generation and MoT denoise need many short guest forwards that attend to an already cached text prefix. Exporting KV for every forward is impractical.

This PR makes each guest forward an ordinary prefill-only `/generate` request. It radix-matches the cached prefix by token IDs and batches through the existing SRT scheduler without model-specific scheduler code. The request is sessionless. A higher-level client owns logical sessions and recovery.

## Request contract

- `input_ids` carries the cached prefix and guest-span placeholder IDs.
- `input_embeds` carries the guest rows inline or in caller-owned shared memory.
- `query_attention: "bidirectional"` lets every guest row attend the full prefix and every row in its guest span.
- `token_positions` supplies explicit `[rows]` or `[dims][rows]` non-negative signed 64-bit positions strictly below the active model context length.
- `sampling_params.max_new_tokens: 0` and `return_hidden_states: true` request a prefill-only forward with last-layer hidden states.
- Optional `hidden_states_buffer` metadata describes an exact `float32 [rows, model_hidden_size]` caller-owned shared-memory segment.

When `hidden_states_buffer` is present, SRT validates the segment, attaches to it, writes the guest rows, closes its attachment, and echoes the same reference in `meta_info.hidden_states`. SRT never creates or unlinks the segment. Without a buffer, hidden states use the existing inline response.

A late attach or write failure returns HTTP 400. It does not fall back to a large inline response or crash the scheduler. The obsolete `hidden_states_transport` field is rejected with migration guidance.

Inline and shared-memory inputs are validated before model execution for shape, width, dtype, finite values, float32 range, and position bounds.

## Scheduler behavior

- Requests use the ordinary waiting queue and batch only with the same attention mode and position dimensionality.
- Internal requests without optional `query_attention` metadata retain causal attention. Explicit mixed modes still reject.
- Prefix matching stops before the guest embeddings, so guest rows never enter radix cache.
- If the full required prefix is no longer cached, the request releases staged resources and returns HTTP 400 with guidance to re-prefill and resubmit.
- A bidirectional guest span is never chunk-split. Oversized spans reject at the API. A batch-boundary split waits until the whole span fits.
- Batched hidden states are sliced by each request's actual extend width.

## Validation

```bash
PYTHONPATH=python python -m pytest \
  test/registered/unit/managers/test_context_forward_helpers.py \
  test/registered/unit/utils/test_shm_transport_utils.py -q
```

- Focused unit matrix: **39 passed and 40 subtests passed**.
- Adjacent schema, IPC, hidden-state, output, and scheduling matrix: **46 passed and 23 subtests passed**.
- The complete registered manager unit directory exited successfully.
- Black, isort, Ruff, AST, and diff checks passed on all 13 changed files.
- The registered FA3 GPU matrix on Qwen3-0.6B passed all 6 tests on the submitted head in 46.00 seconds. The validation-only follow-up did not rerun the GPU matrix.
- Inline and shared-memory outputs had maximum difference 0. Embedding injection reached cosine similarity 1.0. The future-neighbor counterfactual produced a first-row delta of 5.5, proving within-span bidirectionality.
- All 12 prefix tokens were cached, guest rows were not inserted, eviction and reseed recovery passed, and 25 shared-memory lifecycle cycles left no residual caller segments.
- For the audited 256 x 1024 payload, paired shared memory measured 23.267 ms compared with 371.296 ms inline, a 15.958x ratio. Concurrency 1, 2, 4, and 8 reached 57.178, 62.829, 105.371, and 153.255 requests per second with no failures.

items.title: [AMD] perf: fuse Kimi-K2.5 MLA projection, RoPE, and KV-cache write
items.body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

During Kimi-K2.5 MXFP4 graph decode on ROCm gfx95, the absorbed MLA key projection, rotary embedding, and KV-cache write are launched separately on the latency-critical path even though they share operands.

Fusing these operations reduces decode launch overhead and improves long-context serving performance.

## Modifications

- Fuse the absorbed MXFP4 `w_kc` projection, RoPE, and KV-cache write into one AITER grid using `fused_fp4_bmm_rope_cat_and_cache_mla`.
- Add `SGLANG_ROCM_FUSE_MLA_PROJECTION_ROPE_CACHE`, enabled by default.
- Restrict the fast path to ROCm gfx95/AITER graph decode with MXFP4 `w_kc`.
- Validate the fused kernel's shape requirements before dispatch:
  - `kv_lora_rank` must be a power of two.
  - `qk_rope_head_dim` must be a power of two and at least 2.
  - `qk_nope_head_dim` must be a power of two between 32 and 256.
- Retain the existing split path for unsupported configurations, including DSA, DCP, optimized LoRA execution, and active `kv_b_proj` LoRAs.
- Carry the fusion decision from `forward_absorb_prepare` to `forward_absorb_core` through `RocmMlaProjectionFusionPlan`.
- Add CPU unit coverage for backend, graph-decode, and kernel-shape gating.
- Document the new environment variable.

## Accuracy Tests

Hardware and model:

- 4× AMD Instinct MI355X (`gfx950`)
- Model: `Kimi-K2.5-MXFP4`
- TP=4
- AITER prefill and decode attention
- AITER MoE and all-reduce fusion
- FP8 E4M3 KV cache
- Full GSM8K test set: 1,319 questions, 8-shot, maximum 512 new tokens
- Project accuracy threshold: 0.92

| Configuration | Accuracy | Invalid responses | Status |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| Fusion disabled | 0.925 | 0.000 | PASS |
| Fusion enabled | 0.930 | 0.000 | PASS |

The fused path preserved accuracy and remained above the existing 0.92 threshold.

Focused unit tests:

```text
2 passed, 5 subtests passed
```

The tests cover the AITER graph-decode gate and reject unsupported non-power-of-two or out-of-range shapes.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

The A/B benchmark follows the Kimi-K2.5 ROCm recipe.

Configuration:

- 4× AMD Instinct MI355X (`gfx950`)
- Kimi-K2.5 MXFP4, TP=4
- AITER prefill/decode attention and MoE
- AITER all-reduce fusion
- FP8 E4M3 KV cache, page size 16
- Breakable prefill graph and full decode graph
- Maximum concurrency: 4
- ISL: 8,192
- OSL: 1,024
- 20 measured requests after warmup
- Identical seed and generated workload for both arms
- The only A/B feature change was `SGLANG_ROCM_FUSE_MLA_PROJECTION_ROPE_CACHE=0/1`

| Metric | Fusion disabled | Fusion enabled | Change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Output throughput | 428.77 tok/s | 433.33 tok/s | +1.06% |
| Total token throughput | 3,861.04 tok/s | 3,902.11 tok/s | +1.06% |
| Median TPOT | 8.81 ms | 8.68 ms | -1.48% |
| Median end-to-end latency | 8,455.36 ms | 8,328.59 ms | -1.50% |
| Median TTFT | 246.43 ms | 247.99 ms | +0.63% |

The fusion improves decode-sensitive throughput, TPOT, and end-to-end latency for the 8k/1k workload. The small TTFT variation is expected because this optimization targets graph decode rather than prefill.

items.title: [XPU]Enable HiSparse hierarchical sparse KV cache on Intel XPU
items.body:
Enable HiSparse (hierarchical sparse KV cache) on Intel XPU (in addition to CUDA/ROCm), and enable the corresponding unit tests.

The two hot kernels — `load_cache_to_device_buffer_{mla,dsv4_mla}` and `transfer_cache_dsv4_mla` — are ported to SYCL in [sgl-kernel-xpu#335](https://github.com/sgl-project/sgl-kernel-xpu/pull/335). CUDA/ROCm JIT-compiles them via `sglang.kernels.ops.kvcache.hisparse`; the XPU port is AOT-compiled into the `sgl_kernel` wheel.

Source changes:
- `pool_host/common.py`: register `"xpu": alloc_with_pin_memory` in `ALLOC_MEMORY_FUNCS` so XPU uses torch's built-in `pin_memory=True` instead of `cudaHostRegister`.
- `pool_host/mla.py`, `memory_pool_host.py`, `hisparse_memory_pool.py`: widen `if _is_cuda or _is_hip:` to `... or _is_xpu:` so `sgl_kernel.kvcacheio.transfer_kv_all_layer_*` is imported on XPU.
- `hisparse_coordinator.py`, `memory_pool_host.py`: branch the kernel imports explicitly — XPU to `sgl_kernel`, everything else to the JIT ops.

### Supported and Verified following Features

- Swap-in of top-k selected pages (MLA and DSv4 layouts)
- Device-buffer LRU replacement across decode steps
- Long-sequence host-to-device DMA path
- Batched multi-request swap-in with padding
- Request lifecycle: staging path and direct-to-host path
- PD decode host-slot preallocation
- Paged host layout (`page_size` > 1)

### Not supported on XPU

- Shared-index prefetch: `copy_cache_planned_mla` has no AOT SYCL kernel, so it is bound to a raising stub; the coordinator disables prefetch at init with a warning.
- `SGLANG_DEBUG_HISPARSE_SKIP_IO`: `skip_io` is a JIT template parameter baked in at compile time, so the AOT ops do not accept it. Setting the env var on XPU now raises at init instead of silently producing timings that include the KV copy.

Test changes:
- Device-agnostic device selection via `get_device()` / `get_device_module()` and `register_xpu_ci` across the HiSparse kernel and unit tests.

## Motivation

- Intel XPU is a first-class inference target, but HiSparse hard-gates on `is_cuda() or is_hip()` in several places and dispatches host pin-memory allocation through a CUDA-only registrar, so DSA / DeepSeek-V4-class models cannot use hierarchical sparse attention there.
- The SYCL kernels already exist in `sgl-kernel-xpu`; what was missing was the sglang-side wiring, backend gates, and device-agnostic tests.
- Without XPU CI coverage, XPU-specific breakage in the HiSparse paths would go undetected until a user report.

## Modifications

- Registered XPU in `ALLOC_MEMORY_FUNCS` and widened the three `_is_cuda or _is_hip` import gates to admit XPU.
- Branched the swap-in / replay / transfer kernel imports so XPU resolves to the AOT `sgl_kernel` ops and CUDA/ROCm keeps the JIT ops unchanged.
- Made the two XPU-unsupported features fail loudly at init rather than silently no-op.
- Converted the HiSparse kernel and unit tests to `get_device()` / `get_device_module()` and registered them under the XPU CI suite `stage-b-test-1-gpu-xpu`.

## Accuracy Tests

```
$ pytest test/registered/kernels/ops/kvcache/test_hisparse.py
10 passed, 8 skipped

$ pytest test/registered/unit/managers/test_hisparse_unit.py
9 passed, 2 skipped
```

All 10 skips are ROCm-only tests gated on `not is_hip()`; they skip on CUDA as well. The unit tests include the kernel-vs-`naive_load_topk` oracle comparison, so SYCL/CUDA numerical parity is exercised on the same test bodies.

CUDA/ROCm is unaffected on this revision. 

## Speed Tests and Profiling

N/A — enablement only; the CUDA/ROCm hot path is untouched. SYCL kernel benchmarking is tracked in `sgl-kernel-xpu`.

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).

items.title: [Feature] MXFP4 KV Cache Decode for DSV4 on Hopper
items.body:
## Summary

MXFP4 KV cache for DeepSeek V4 on Hopper (SM90/H20), end to end: codec + memory pool + fused decode attention kernel + backend integration. The decode kernel is a JIT-compiled port of the FlashMLA three-stage split-KV design (scheduler metadata kernel + persistent WGMMA main kernel + combine kernel), covering all 44 layers (SWA + C4/C128 + attn_sink) in one call.

The PR is self-contained: the kernel and its vendored dependencies live under `python/sglang/kernels/jit/` and compile at first use via `load_jit` — no sgl-kernel wheel changes required.

## MXFP4 Layout (368 B/token)

```
[224 B packed E2M1 | 14 B E8M0 + 2 B pad | 128 B BF16 RoPE]
```

- E2M1 (4-bit FP: 1S+2E+1M) nope data, block-size 32 (14 groups)
- E8M0 8-bit exponent-only scale per group (dequantized in-register via `bits << 23`)
- BF16 RoPE (unquantized)
- Row-major contiguous, no page tail padding; no global scale needed (unlike NVFP4)
- 16-byte-aligned row (368 B = 16×23) enables 128-bit loads; the NVFP4 reference's 380 B is only 4-byte aligned

Memory capacity gain vs FP8: ~+37% full-token capacity (bytes/token 7705 → 5609; the NVFP4 reference gains +31.75%).

## Decode Kernel (`kernels/jit/csrc/mxfp4_dsv4_decode_sm90/`)

FlashMLA-style fused split-KV decode for MXFP4:

1. **Scheduler metadata kernel** — 1 CTA × 1 thread computes per-SM split assignments with device-side length clamping (CUDA-graph safe: runs inside the captured graph, re-executes with replayed top-k lengths)
2. **Persistent main kernel** — 384 threads (3 warp groups: producer dequant→SMEM, QK+PV local, PV remote), WGMMA 64×64×16 / 64×256×16; E8M0 block-32 dequant via bit-shift, E2M1 via LUT+PRMT (4 instructions per 16 elements)
3. **Combine kernel** — merges split-K partials with PDL (programmatic dependent launch)

Entry point: `entry.cuh` (TVM-FFI single translation unit, explicit instantiations for h_q 64/128). Python wrapper: `kernels/ops/attention/mxfp4_dsv4_decode_sm90.py` (FlashMLASchedMeta, per-geometry scratch reuse, C++-side stream resolution via `TVMFFIEnvGetStream`).

### Vendored dependencies (provenance)

| Component | Source |
|---|---|
| `params.h`, `defines.h`, `utils.h`, `flashmla_utils.h`, `kerutils/`, `combine` | FlashMLA upstream @ 05e26647 |
| `config.h`, `dequant.h`, `layout.h`, `components/helpers.h`, splitkv skeleton | SGLang reference PR #31269 (NVFP4) |
| `splitkv_mla.cuh` (MXFP4 variant), `entry.cuh` | This PR |

CUTLASS/CUTE headers come from the JIT build's `extra_dependencies=["cutlass"]` (pinned cutlass @ 147f5673, matching the reference PR). `kerutils` includes were converted to relative paths during vendoring.

## Changes

- **Codec** (`srt/layers/attention/dsv4/mxfp4_k_cache.py`): quantize/dequant for the 368 B row (Triton), paged variants
- **Compressor** (`compressor_v2.py`): `_forward_mxfp4` covering all 44 layers (C0/C4/C128), decode-plan boundary semantics
- **Memory pool**: parameterized enablement via `--kv-cache-dtype fp4_e2m1 --fp4-kv-cache-recipe mxfp4` (env alias with deprecation warning); pool sizing/accounting unified
- **Startup guards**: HiSparse + MXFP4 combination rejected at init (incompatible sparse layout); DeepseekV4 + fp4_e2m1 on non-SM90 fails fast with a clear error
- **Backend** (`deepseek_v4_backend.py`): `_forward_mxfp4_decode_flashmla` — one fused call per layer; scheduler metadata shared per geometry across layers, re-created during CUDA-graph capture (top-k lengths are replayed device inputs)
- **Tests**: `test/registered/kernels/ops/attention/test_mxfp4_dsv4_decode.py` (17 kernel cases: C0/C4/C128 × flash/profiling geometries, graph replay + length clamping, invalid contracts, scheduler-refresh regressions) + `test_mxfp4_k_cache.py` (5 codec cases) + `test_dsv4_hisparse_pool.py` (3 pool-guard cases) + `test_dsv4_compress_write_pad.py` (3 restored cases); benchmark in `test/registered/kernels/benchmark/attention/bench_mxfp4_dsv4_decode.py`
- **E2E**: `test/registered/kernels/e2e/test_mxfp4_dsv4_e2e.py` — 8-GPU H200 server + gsm8k, exercising pool configurator → compressor → CUDA-graph capture (CI stage extra-b)
- Removed the first-generation standalone JIT kernel (`mxfp4_decode.cuh` + `_forward_mxfp4_decode`) superseded by the FlashMLA port

## Validation

- Kernel SASS was byte-identical to the AOT (cmake) build of the same sources at port time; the subsequent refactors (V32 path removal, aligned 128-bit row loads) are instruction-level changes covered by the same unit suite
- Unit: 28/28 kernel + codec + pool-guard tests pass; 8-GPU e2e integration test passes locally
- End-to-end on 8×H20 (TP8, `DeepSeek-V4-Flash`), FP8 (`--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3`) vs MXFP4 (`--kv-cache-dtype fp4_e2m1 --fp4-kv-cache-recipe mxfp4`), identical server flags otherwise:

| Metric | FP8 baseline | MXFP4 (this PR) | Δ |
|---|---|---|---|
| Decode throughput (server-side, 4k×256, conc 32) | 1013 tok/s | 980 tok/s | −3.3% |
| GSM8K (1319, greedy, max_tokens 1024; truncated samples excluded) | 96.89% | 96.89% | 0.0pt |
| AIME25 (480 = 30×16, greedy, max_tokens 32768; 73 truncated samples excluded from both) | 99.57% pass@1 | 99.78% pass@1 | +0.2pt |

## Known gaps / follow-ups

- Small-batch (b≤8) kernel-level latency vs FP8: +8–12% (kernel-inherent scheduling granularity; end-to-end TPOT already within 5%)
- Prefill-path throughput: −6.8% vs FP8 (out of scope for this PR; triton-based MXFP4 prefill)
- Deep-context + high-concurrency decode (64 concurrent, 8k ctx, no rolling prefill): decode TPOT +17% vs FP8 (33.1 vs 28.3 ms); end-to-end 8k→8k throughput on par (1677 vs 1652 tok/s). One full AIME25 eval run showed −44% throughput vs FP8, but four controlled reruns (5-question replica, rolling short-prompt, 8k×8k fixed) could not reproduce it and measured MXFP4 at parity or faster — attributed to environment, not the kernel.
- sm_90a-only (Hopper); no SM100 support (non-SM90 + fp4_e2m1 is rejected at startup)
- HiSparse (sparse KV cache) not supported with MXFP4 — rejected at startup

## References

- PR #31269 — NVFP4 KV cache for DSV4 in sgl-kernel (reference implementation for the FlashMLA three-stage decode)
- FlashMLA upstream @ 05e26647 — scheduler/combine kernels and kerutils
- This PR takes the jit_kernel approach (JIT CUDA via TVM-FFI) instead of AOT CUTLASS in sgl-kernel, keeping the PR self-contained

---

**Status**: Ready for review — kernel + integration complete, end-to-end validated on 8×H20.

items.title: Free draft's duplicate embed/lm_head before KV cache sizing
items.body:
## Problem

With EAGLE/NEXTN the draft model loads its own `embed_tokens` and `lm_head`, and `init_lm_head()` then frees them and repoints the draft at the target's tensors. Both calls sit at the end of `EagleDraftWorker.alloc_memory_pool()`, which the scheduler only reaches after `init_target_memory_pool()` has already profiled free VRAM to size the KV cache:

```python
def init_memory_pools(self):
    self.init_target_memory_pool()                 # profiles free memory here
    if self.draft_worker is not None:
        self.draft_worker.alloc_memory_pool(...)   # frees the duplicates here
```

So the duplicate vocab tensors are resident when free memory is measured, and are released a moment later into a budget that is already fixed.

At vocab 248320 and hidden size 5120 each of these tensors is 2.54 GB. The target already carries 5.1 GB of them by itself, and the draft's copies take the resident total to roughly 10 GB of vocabulary weights while the profile runs. The draft's half is what never reaches the KV pool.

## Fix

Move `init_token_map()` / `init_lm_head()` into `EagleDraftWorker.__init__`. Both models are constructed by the end of `__init__` and neither call touches a memory pool.

`torch.cuda.empty_cache()` is load-bearing rather than cosmetic: `set_embed_and_head` only drops the Parameter references, and without an explicit release the blocks stay in the caching allocator, where `get_available_gpu_memory()` still counts them as used.

## Test

Qwen3.6-27B (vocab 248320, hybrid GDN + attention), NEXTN, `--mem-fraction-static 0.93` unchanged throughout.

Sweeping `vocab_size` with `--load-format dummy` (32k / 128k / 200k / 248k), the KV cache recovered by the patch tracks `2 * vocab * hidden * dtype` to within 0.5%, so what comes back is exactly the two duplicated tensors. Dummy weights make this reproducible without the checkpoint.

`max_total_num_tokens`, same flags on either side:

- H800 80GB, dummy weights on an otherwise idle card: 258395 -> 336027. A real-weight run reproduced the patched figure exactly.
- V100 32GB: 2297 -> 21715 (where this turned up; a small card is just where it stops being invisible)

Greedy output is byte-identical before and after (128 tokens, temperature 0), as expected for a change that only moves when an existing assignment happens.

EAGLE3 recovers about half as much (236208 -> 272741, dummy weights). Drafts that set their own `draft_vocab_size`, which per the comment in `init_lm_head` is the common case, take the `set_embed()` path and share only the embedding, keeping their own lm_head by design. 

No new unit test. The change is a pure move with no new identifiers or config, and the existing EAGLE/MTP tests already cover the sharing path; the effect it fixes is a VRAM accounting one that needs a GPU to observe.

Related but a different root cause: #29857 / #30092, where the per-token cell size is inflated by a config attribute fallback.

items.title: [MHA] Support HND KV cache layout in CPU offload
items.body:
## Motivation

CPU KV cache offloading previously assumed that each token slot was stored as a contiguous row in NHD layout. When `SGLANG_USE_HND_KVCACHE` was enabled,
`get_cpu_copy` and `load_cpu_copy` rejected CPU offloading because HND stores a token slot as `[page, head, offset, dim]`.

This PR adds CPU offloading support for HND KV cache layout while preserving existing NHD behavior.

## Modifications

- Support gathering HND KV cache slots into NHD-shaped CPU tensors during offloading.
- Support scattering CPU tensors back into the corresponding HND page and offset during loading.
- Preserve chunked CPU offloading and asymmetric K/V head dimensions.
- Include quantized KV cache scale buffers in NHD CPU copies.
- Explicitly reject the unsupported combination of HND layout and quantized KV cache.
- Update SWA CPU-copy filtering to preserve all tensors in each chunk, including quantization scales.
- Add unit tests for:
  - NHD and HND round trips.
  - HND with page sizes 1 and 4.
  - Asymmetric K/V head dimensions.
  - Chunked CUDA transfers.
  - Quantized NHD data and scale restoration.
  - SWA filtering with quantized scale chunks.
  - Rejection of HND with quantized KV cache.

## Accuracy Tests

This change does not modify attention computation or model arithmetic.

Round-trip tests use exact sentinel comparisons to verify that K/V data and quantization scales are restored without modification.

Tests were run on an NVIDIA L20 GPU:

- PR-specific CPU offload tests: `9 passed`
- Memory pool, layout, and quantized KV cache tests: `39 passed`
- SWA memory pool and lifecycle tests: `38 passed`, plus `18 subtests passed`
- FP4 KV cache tests: `16 passed, 1 skipped`
  - The skipped test requires Blackwell NVFP4 support and is expected on L20.
- Additional CUDA integration checks:
  - Quantized NHD data and scale CPU round trip: passed.
  - Quantized SWA partial-mapping data and scale round trip: passed.

Overall pytest result: `102 passed, 1 expected skip`.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

N/A. This change only affects CPU KV cache offload and restore operations and does not modify the inference hot path.

## Checklist

- [x] Format the code with `pre-commit run --all-files --show-diff-on-failure`.
- [x] Add unit tests for the modified behavior.
- [x] Documentation update is not required because no user-facing API or configuration is added.

items.title: [hicache] Propagate override_kv_cache_dim to the draft host KV pool
items.body:
## Motivation

`maybe_register_hicache_draft()` creates the draft host KV pool with the same
slot count as the target host pool, and the comment states the intent:

```python
# Create host pool for draft with the same slot count as the target host pool,
# so that host indices stay 1-to-1 between target and draft KV caches.
```

The per-token **stride** is not kept in sync, though. The target host pool can be
constructed with `override_kv_cache_dim` (see `build_kv_host_pool()` in
`hybrid_pool_assembler.py`), which is how the scaled fp8 KV layout is expressed:
`kv_lora_rank + kv_lora_rank // quant_block_size * 4 + qk_rope_head_dim *
rope_storage_dtype.itemsize`.

`maybe_register_hicache_draft()` does not forward it, so `MLATokenToKVPoolHost`
falls back to its default in `get_size_per_token()`:

```python
self.kv_cache_dim = self.override_kv_cache_dim or (
    self.kv_lora_rank + self.qk_rope_head_dim
)
```

Result: with fp8 KV + hierarchical cache + a draft (MTP/EAGLE) worker, the target
and draft host pools disagree on bytes-per-token while their host indices are
1-to-1 by construction. A host index therefore addresses slots of two different
sizes on the two sides.

The failure is layout-dependent rather than immediate: light load mostly touches
the region where the two strides still overlap, so it surfaces as sporadic
garbage in restored draft KV, and as batched host↔device copy failures once
enough concurrent requests push transfers past the smaller stride. This matches
the symptom reported in #31600 (fp8 KV + L2/L3 hierarchical cache), which has no
fix on `main` today.

## Modification

Forward the target host pool's `override_kv_cache_dim` when constructing the
draft host pool, so both sides derive the same per-token stride.

Scoped to the MLA branch, since `override_kv_cache_dim` is an
`MLATokenToKVPoolHost` parameter. `getattr(..., None)` keeps the call safe for
target pools that were built without an override — that path is unchanged.

## Tests

Added `TestDraftHostPoolStrideParity` to
`test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_dsa_pool_host_unit.py`, alongside the
existing DSA host-pool unit tests and using the same fixture and CUDA/ROCm
guards.

It asserts that a draft host pool built with the target's override reports the
same `get_size_per_token()` as the target, and — so the parity assertion cannot
pass for the wrong reason — that dropping the override changes it.

## Checklist

- [x] Behavior is unchanged when the target pool has no override (`None` is the
      existing default).
- [x] No new configuration or flags.
- [x] Unit test added next to the existing host-pool tests.

items.title: [Feature] OSCAR mixed-precision INT2 KV cache (--kv-cache-dtype int2)
items.body:
## Motivation

This PR adds **OSCAR** (Offline Spectral Covariance-Aware Rotation), a mixed-precision **INT2 KV cache** ([paper](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2605.17757), [project page](https://oscar-quantize.github.io/)): the bulk of the KV cache is stored as 2-bit codes (packed 4-per-byte with per-group scale/zero pairs) while a small BF16 sink prefix and rolling recent window stay high-precision. This cuts KV memory by **~8× vs BF16** at near-BF16 quality, which translates into much longer contexts / larger batches per GPU, and higher decode throughput once batches are KV-capacity-bound.

Headline quality numbers from the paper's protocol (mean of GPQA / HumanEval / LCB v6 / AIME25 / MATH-500, 5 seeds, 32K gen):

| Method | BPE | Qwen3-4B Thinking | Qwen3-8B | Qwen3-32B | GLM-4.7-FP8 (358B) |
|:---|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|
| BF16 (upper bound) | 16.00 | 75.64 | 70.84 | 74.19 | 77.89 |
| QuaRot-INT2 | 2.25 | 1.40 | 10.14 | 7.90 | 75.14 |
| **OSCAR** | **2.28** | **71.86** | **69.42** | **74.17** | **78.16** |

Everything is **opt-in behind `--kv-cache-dtype int2`** (plus an optional `--kv-cache-quant-group-size`); default behavior is byte-identical for existing users.

## Modifications

**New components**
- `UnifiedInt2HPKVPool` / `UnifiedInt2HPKVAllocator` (`srt/mem_cache/unified_kv_{pool,allocator}.py`): paged INT2 quant arena + shared HP-prefix pool + per-request HP-recent rings in one flat slot-id namespace (kernels dispatch on `slot >= HP_OFFSET`). `--page-size` is auto-set to the quant page size `N_Q` so radix-tree splits land on physical page boundaries.
- `sglang/QuantKernel/`: fused rotate→clip→quantize→pack Triton kernels (offline-calibrated per-layer rotations with a data-free Hadamard fallback), optional Lloyd-Max MSE-optimal buckets (`SGLANG_LLOYD_MAX`), and the decode-time GPU flush that demotes tokens leaving the HP-recent window into the quant tier (plan/apply split so host syncs don't stall behind the previous forward).
- `srt/layers/attention/quantized_kv_prefill.py`: shared rotation-aware prefill helpers (prefix dequant, Q/K/V pre-rotation, V-inverse).
- INT2 decode kernels in `kernels/ops/attention/decode_attention.py`: quantized stage-1 (grouped + non-grouped) and a single-launch mixed-tier path that reduces HP and dequantized-INT2 splits in one LSE-based stage-2.

**Integration points (gated on int2 / mixed-KV enabled)**
- `KVCacheConfigurator`: int2 pool/allocator construction; `pool_configurator`: quant-token cell-size accounting.
- Triton backend: mixed-tier decode dispatch + per-tier metadata (Triton index-build kernels, no host sync); CUDA-graph capture/replay via the shared graph-metadata funnel, padded writes routed to the reserved HP page.
- FA3 backend: rotation-aware int2 prefill for the hybrid `--prefill-attention-backend fa3 --decode-attention-backend triton` configuration (K/V pre-rotated once, written with `already_hadamard_transformed=True`).
- Scheduler/radix: mixed-KV extend/decode allocation (page-aligned quant-slack ownership, per-request flush counters), radix match cap excluding per-request HP-recent slot ids, ownership clamps at partial quant pages, forward-done event stashing for flush ordering.
- Env knobs registered in `environ.py` (`SGLANG_OSCAR_*`, `SGLANG_MIXED_KV_*`, `SGLANG_INT2_*`, `SGLANG_LLOYD_MAX`, `SGLANG_HADAMARD_ORDER`).

**Usage**

```bash
SGLANG_ENABLE_MIXED_KV_WINDOWS=1 \
SGLANG_OSCAR_K_ROTATION_PATH=.../k_rotation_qqt_r_h_pbr.pt \
SGLANG_OSCAR_V_ROTATION_PATH=.../v_rotation_sst_r_h_pbr.pt \
SGLANG_OSCAR_K_CLIP_RATIO=0.96 SGLANG_OSCAR_V_CLIP_RATIO=0.92 \
SGLANG_OSCAR_ABSORB_V_ROTATION=1 \
SGLANG_MIXED_KV_PREFIX_TOKENS=64 SGLANG_MIXED_KV_RECENT_TOKENS=256 \
python -m sglang.launch_server --model-path Qwen/Qwen3-8B \
  --kv-cache-dtype int2 --kv-cache-quant-group-size 128 \
  --prefill-attention-backend fa3 --decode-attention-backend triton \
  --max-running-requests 64
```

Pre-computed rotations for several models are on HF ([`Zhongzhu/OSCAR-RotationZoo`](https://huggingface.co/Zhongzhu/OSCAR-RotationZoo)); the calibration pipeline (dump → fit, ~20 min for an 8B model on one H100) lives in the [OSCAR repo](https://github.com/FutureMLS-Lab/OSCAR).

## Accuracy / validation

Qwen3-8B, single H100, official RotationZoo rotation, GPQA-Diamond (198 Q), temp 1.0 / top-p 0.95 / top-k 40 / 32K max gen, 32 concurrent:

| Build | GPQA-Diamond |
|---|---|
| research fork (source of this port) | 56.06 (111/198) |
| **this PR on current main** | **57.07 (113/198)** |

(Δ within single-seed noise; SE ≈ 3.5pp.) An 8.6K-token needle-retrieval probe returns the needle exactly through the INT2 quant tier on **both** supported attention configurations (fa3-prefill + triton-decode, and pure triton). No crashes across the full eval (198 requests, chunked prefill + decode flush + request churn).

## Current scope / limitations

- Attention backends: Triton decode required; prefill = FA3 or Triton. Other backends fall back to rejecting int2 at startup with a clear error.
- Mixed HP windows currently exclude: speculative decoding, PD-disaggregation, DCP, hybrid-SWA models, and sink tokens in decode (each guarded explicitly).
- The shared HP-prefix pool defaults to `req_slots × prefix_tokens × 16` slots and is not yet folded into the mem-fraction profile — deployments should set `--max-running-requests` (or `SGLANG_MIXED_KV_HP_PREFIX_POOL_TOKENS`); a follow-up can move this into the profiled budget.
- MLA models are out of scope here (a separate line of work).

Happy to split this into a stacked series (pool/kernels → backends → scheduler integration) if reviewers prefer.

items.title: [Feat][DeepSeek V4] Shared KV Cache for Prefill CP
items.body:
## Motivation

DeepSeek V4 Prefill context parallelism requires every CP rank to access the complete attention history. The ordinary layout keeps persistent KV replicated across CP ranks and limits long-context capacity. Following the Shared-KV direction introduced in #31435, this PR stores each attention page on one CP owner while exposing one logical address view to all ranks through CUDA VMM.

## Modifications

- Add reusable Shared-KV primitives for owner-sharded CUDA VMM storage, logical-to-physical layout, publication, transfer, and row Demand-cache.
- Add a thin DeepSeek V4 adapter for owner-sharded SWA/C4/C128 KV and mutable attention compression state. Indexer KV/state remain rank-local replicas.
- Use FlashMLA-KV for Prefill and Decode. SM90 and SM100 Prefill use a transient, capacity-guarded one-way Demand-cache; Decode keeps the minimal direct VMM view. Null-cache calls preserve the original FlashMLA direct-read kernels.
- Support owner-sharded Prefill-PD transfer and add focused common, DSV4, PD, layout, capacity, and numerical tests.

## Validation

Validated on one 8 x NVIDIA H20 node with DeepSeek-V4-Flash-FP8, CP8TP8, FP8 E4M3 KV, FlashMLA-KV Prefill/Decode, page size 256, 8,192-token chunks, and 16,384 maximum Prefill tokens. The 128K/B1 result is the mean of three warmed, cache-flushed runs with identical arguments other than the Shared flag.

| Workload | Base CP8 TTFT | Shared KV TTFT | Shared vs Base |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 128K / B1 | 4,336.64 ms | 4,398.78 ms | +1.43% |

The owner-sharded persistent attention cache is single-copy across CP8. The transient Prefill Demand-cache uses 629,145,600 bytes per rank; its storage is reused across layers, but every layer starts a fresh epoch and retains no cross-layer or cross-request validity.

The fixed-base release commit passes 290 focused tests plus 90 subtests. Seven SM90 FlashMLA GPU tests produce Base-vs-Demand bit-exact output/LSE, including a 37,376-byte Shared source stride, and the fixed 32K Base/Shared precision case has identical top-1 output with 19/20 top-logprob token overlap. A final 128K/B1/output=1 Shared smoke completed successfully. The FlashMLA extension builds dedicated Demand-cache and direct-read cubins for SM90 and SM100 with CUDA 13; B200 correctness and performance validation remain pending because the available cluster contains only H20/H20-3e nodes.

## Status

- [x] Reusable Shared-KV/VMM and Demand-cache foundation
- [x] DeepSeek-V4-Flash-FP8 on SM90 with CP8TP8
- [x] FlashMLA-KV Prefill and basic Decode
- [x] SM90 transient Prefill Demand-cache
- [x] SM100 transient Prefill Demand-cache source and CUDA13 build support
- [x] Owner-sharded Prefill-PD path and regression coverage
- [x] Correctness, numerical, capacity, and warmed Prefill validation
- [ ] Decode performance optimization
- [ ] B200/SM100 end-to-end and performance validation
- [ ] DeepSeek-V4-Pro-FP8 validation
- [ ] Owner-sharded L2/L3
- [ ] Speculative decoding and PP support

Enable with `--enable-dsa-shared-kv-cache`.

Co-authored with [@foraxe](https://github.com/foraxe)

items.title: [Feature] KVarN: KV-cache compression for hybrid linear-attention models
items.body:
## Motivation

Hybrid linear-attention models (GDN/Mamba + full-attention) like Qwen 3.5 and Kimi-Linear have O(n) linear-attention layers but still retain O(n²) full-attention layers whose KV cache dominates GPU memory at long contexts. This limits the practical context length on commodity GPUs (e.g. 24 GB RTX 3090). KVarN compresses the full-attention KV cache to int4 (~8x reduction vs BF16), enabling long-context inference within bounded GPU memory.

## Modifications

### Core design

**Quantization pipeline**: Per-tile Hadamard rotation → Sinkhorn variance normalization → 4-bit packing with per-group scales. K and V are compressed independently (`k4v4` or `k4v2` presets, configurable group size). Dequant is fused into the attention kernel, avoiding a separate dequant pass.

**Attention backend** (`kvarn_backend.py`): A dedicated attention backend that manages a dual-pool architecture:
- Compressed int4 pool: the long-term cache, sized by the pool configurator at the compressed per-token cost.
- Tail fp16 pool: a small sliding window of recent tokens kept at full precision, flushed to int4 when the window slides.

**Triton kernels** (`kvarn_ops/`): Custom decode and sinkhorn kernels for the compressed attention path. The decode kernel fuses dequant with QK^T and attention.

**HiCache integration**: KVarN stores raw int4 tiles in the host memory pool (~2.7 KB/token) without dequant/requant, enabling transparent offloading of long conversation history. A new `_KVarNNopaStrategy` is registered in the hybrid cache assembler.

### Memory pool sizing

- `KVCacheConfigurator` and `DefaultPoolConfigurator` recognize the `kvarn_*` cache dtype and size the pool at the compressed per-token cost (`tile_bytes * num_heads / group`) with a 30% overhead for the tail pool and runtime allocations.
- Mamba cache sizing is capped for KVarN hybrid models to prevent the scheduler from over-allocating the linear-attention component.
- Transient prefill workspace is reserved in `_profile_available_bytes` (`chunk * hidden * dtype * 20`, target worker only) to prevent latent OOM during large-chunk prefill.
- `SGLANG_HICACHE_HOST_MEMORY_RESERVE_GB` env var (default 10.0) makes the HiCache host-memory reserve tunable. Previously hardcoded to 10 GB, which blocked HiCache on hosts with limited free RAM.

### Speculative decoding compatibility

- DFlash/EAGLE draft models can target KVarN-compressed models. The draft KV pool is sized at its real per-token cost via `compute_dflash_draft_kv_cell_size_per_token`, computed lazily in the pool configurator once the parallel state is available.
- `--speculative-draft-kv-cache-dtype` flag (default `"auto"`) allows explicit control over the draft model's KV cache dtype. Previously hardcoded; now configurable for cases where the draft uses a different dtype than the target (e.g. fp8 draft behind a KVarN target).
- DFlash draft HiCache is skipped (`maybe_register_hicache_draft` returns early) because the compact draft window never evicts, making a host pool pointless.
- Graph-capturable fused verify path for KVarN targets: the verify `ForwardBatch` is populated with correct `extend_seq_lens` / `prefix_lens` / `extend_lens`, and the target verify CUDA graph capture is skipped for KVarN (the fused verify path handles it).

### Documentation

- Added KVarN section to `docs_new/docs/advanced_features/attention_backend.mdx` with presets table, architecture overview, and usage examples.
- Updated `docs_new/docs/advanced_features/server_arguments.mdx` with `kvarn_*` presets for `--kv-cache-dtype` and the new `--speculative-draft-kv-cache-dtype` flag.

### Files

- **30 new files**: KVarN attention backend, Triton kernels, quantization modules (config, dequant, flush_manager, hadamard, sinkhorn, store)
- **4 modified files**: server_args, environ, attention_registry, mem_cache integration
- **2 docs files**: attention_backend.mdx, server_arguments.mdx
- **1 test file**: extends existing `test_pool_configurator.py` with KVarN-specific cases

## Accuracy Tests

KVarN preserves attention correctness through Hadamard + Sinkhorn preprocessing before 4-bit quantization. The `test_pool_configurator.py` unit tests verify pool sizing invariants (tokens * per_token_cost <= available_bytes). Standalone CPU unit tests for config, sinkhorn, store, dequant, flush, and hadamard modules are in a separate artifacts branch and will be submitted as a follow-up PR after converting them to the `register_cpu_ci` pattern.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

### Single GPU — RTX 3090 (24 GB)

**Qwen 3.5 9B** (KVarN k4v4_g128, no speculative decoding):
- 817K token KV pool, ~70 tok/s decode (CUDA graphs active)
- HiCache 4 GB host pool with `SGLANG_HICACHE_HOST_MEMORY_RESERVE_GB=2`
- 15-turn agentic multi-turn test (context growing 0–57K tokens): passes, server stable

**Qwen 3.5 9B** (KVarN + DFlash speculative decoding):
- Accept length 3–7.6, 105–208 tok/s decode with CUDA graphs active
- Note: DFlash decode is faster, but e2e agentic latency is higher because per-turn draft prefill + verify overhead scales with context length. DFlash is not recommended for short-turn agentic workloads; KVarN-only is the better deployment for that use case.

### Multi-GPU — 2× RTX 3090 (48 GB)

**Qwen 3.5 27B** (KVarN k4v4_g128, TP=2): deployed, serving real agentic load.
**Qwen 3.5 35B** (KVarN k4v4_g128, TP=2): deployed, serving real agentic load.

Both run with KVarN-only (no DFlash) + HiCache. The int4 compression makes these models fit in 2×24 GB with long context, which is not feasible with BF16 or FP8 KV cache.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [x] Update documentation according to the [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Review and Merge Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.
   - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci`
4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR.

Split out of #31879 (general per-tier hit counters only, no UMBP-specific or eviction/load-back changes).

Re-adds the per-tier cache hit breakdown that was previously reverted in `feat/umbp-pr` (001e9ce957) and never carried forward: `PrefillAdder` tracks L1 (GPU device), L2 (host DRAM), and L3 (storage) hit tokens plus cache misses, reported via `SchedulerStats` and exported as `sglang:cache_hit_tokens_l{1,2,3}_total` / `cache_miss_tokens_total` Prometheus counters. items.title: [Fix] Align KV cache eviction priority direction with scheduler when --schedule-low-priority-values-first is enabled
items.body:
## Motivation

When `--schedule-low-priority-values-first` is enabled, the scheduler and 
KV cache eviction use **opposite** priority directions:
- **Scheduler**: lower value = higher priority → scheduled first
- **Cache eviction (PriorityStrategy)**: lower value = evicted first (min-heap)

This means the scheduler's most-preferred requests have their KV cache 
evicted earliest — a cross-component semantic inconsistency.

No existing PR addresses this (confirmed via code/PR search on main).

## Modifications

1. **`evict_policy.py`**: `PriorityStrategy` accepts `low_values_first` param, 
   negating the eviction key when enabled
2. **`utils.py`**: `get_eviction_strategy` passes `low_values_first` through
3. **`cache_init_params.py`**: add `schedule_low_priority_values_first` field
4. **`kv_cache_builder.py`**: wire `ServerArgs` → `CacheInitParams`
5. **`radix_cache.py`**: add `_aggregate_priority` (min for low-values-first, 
   max otherwise), fix root sentinel, replace bare `max()` calls
6. **`hiradix_cache.py`**: use inherited `_aggregate_priority` for shared nodes
7. **`unified_radix_cache.py`**: same aggregation fix + root sentinel
8. **`test_evict_policy.py`**: add `TestPriorityStrategyLowValuesFirst` (3 tests)

## Checklist

- [x] Format code according to the contribution guide
- [x] Add unit tests (`26/26` evict_policy tests passing, including 3 new)
- [ ] Update documentation (N/A — behavior change only under explicit flag)
- [ ] Benchmark (N/A — pure logic fix, no kernel or forward-pass changes)

items.title: [XPU] Fix Encoder Decoder KV Cache Alignment
items.body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

Encoder Decoder models produces garbage output on the intel_xpu backend (page_size > 1). Two root causes in the paged encoder-decoder KV path:

1. Cross-attention page table not converted to page numbers. encoder_page_table was left token-granular while the paged kernel interprets its entries as page indices — the decoder attended to wrong encoder KV.
2. Decoder KV region not page-aligned. e.g. whisper reserves max_source_positions (1500) encoder slots, but 1500 % page_size ≠ 0, so the decoder KV started mid-page. The paged decode kernel/allocator assume each sequence begins on a page boundary (physical slot = page * page_size + i % page_size), so decoder tokens were read/written at wrong slots.

## Modifications

Reserve a page-aligned number of encoder slots (ceil_align(encoder_len, page_size), e.g. 1500 → 1536) so the decoder KV starts on a page boundary, while keeping the true encoder length (1500) for what the encoder writes and what cross-attention reads. The extra padding slots are allocated but never written/read.

- whisper.py — pad_input_ids prepends ceil_align(encoder_len, page_size) dummy tokens; num_image_tokens stays the true length.
- schedule_batch.py — strip/offset the decoder region by the page-aligned reserve; write encoder KV for only the true length.
- mem_cache/allocation.py (alloc_for_decode) — read last_loc and write decoder KV at the page-aligned encoder_offset column.
- xpu_backend.py — stride+divide encoder_page_table into page numbers (cross-attn fix); slice the decoder self-attention page_table from the aligned offset.


All changes use ceil_align(x, page_size), which is the identity when page_size == 1. CUDA Whisper (flashinfer, page_size=1) and every other model are byte-identical no-ops. The paged encoder-decoder decode path is only exercised on XPU today.

items.title: feat: KVarN KV-cache compression for long-context inference
items.body:
## Motivation

Long-context inference is memory-bound: the KV cache grows linearly with sequence length, limiting the number of concurrent requests and the maximum context length on memory-constrained GPUs. KVarN (KV-cache Adaptive Rotation and Normalization) compresses the KV cache ~4x, enabling long-context serving on GPUs that would otherwise be unable to handle it.

## Modifications

KVarN applies three transformations to the KV cache:
1. **Hadamard rotation** of Q, K, V before attention and storage (energy compaction — concentrates signal into fewer components)
2. **Sinkhorn variance normalization** before quantization (balances variance across groups for better int4 packing)
3. **Asymmetric RTN int4 quantization** with per-group scales and zero-points (K and V can have different bit widths)

### Dual-pool architecture

- **Tail pool** (fp16, small): stores rotated K/V for in-progress blocks and sink blocks (first page preserved to prevent tool schema loss)
- **Compressed cache** (int4): stores flushed full blocks as packed uint8 tiles

When a block fills, it is flushed from the tail pool to the compressed cache. Decode uses a fused Triton kernel that dequantizes on-the-fly. Prefill uses a build_packed_kv Triton kernel + `flash_attn_varlen` (memory-efficient, no O(context²) allocation).

### New files

- `layers/quantization/kvarn/`: config, store, dequant, sinkhorn, hadamard, flush_manager (pure PyTorch, unit-testable on CPU)
- `layers/attention/kvarn_backend.py`: `KVarNAttnBackend` — attention backend with dual-pool management
- `layers/attention/kvarn_ops/`: Triton decode + sinkhorn kernels (split-K flash-decoding, auto-enabled at ≥16 blocks when `B*Hk ≤ SM_count`)
- `tests/kvarn/`: 8 test files — CPU unit tests (Hadamard, Sinkhorn, store/dequant roundtrip, pipeline, flush) + GPU tests (Triton kernels, E2E, pool)

### Modified files

- `server_args.py`: KVarN prefill CUDA graph disable rules, `kv_cache_dtype` choices
- `arg_groups/overrides.py`: KVarN attention backend + `page_size` auto-selection
- `mem_cache/memory_pool.py`: `NoOpMHATokenToKVPool` with `_kvarn_backend` hook for hybrid GDN models
- `mem_cache/pool_host/mha.py`: `KVarNHostKVCache` for HiCache (stores raw uint8 int4 tiles)
- `mem_cache/kv_cache_configurator.py`: `_build_kvarn_kv_pool` method
- `mem_cache/hybrid_cache/hybrid_pool_assembler.py`: `_KVarNNopaStrategy`
- `model_executor/pool_configurator.py`: KVarN cell_size calculation
- `configs/mamba_utils.py`: conv_dtype matches model dtype fix
- `models/utils.py`: exclude NoOp pool from fused `set_kv_buffer`
- `layers/attention/attention_registry.py`: `register_attention_backend("kvarn")`
- `mem_cache/kv_cache_dtype.py`: KVarN dtype entries

### Supported presets

| Preset | K bits | V bits | Group |
|--------|--------|--------|-------|
| `kvarn_k4v2_g128` | 4 | 2 | 128 |
| `kvarn_k4v4_g128` | 4 | 4 | 128 |
| `kvarn_k4v2_g64` | 4 | 2 | 64 |
| `kvarn_k4v4_g64` | 4 | 4 | 64 |

### Integration

Works with:
- Hybrid GDN models (e.g. Qwen3.6-27B: 16 full-attention + 48 mamba/GDN layers)
- Hierarchical cache (HiCache) with write-back policy
- CUDA graph for decode path
- Mixed-chunk scheduling
- Tool calling (block-0 sink preservation)
- Speculative decoding verify path

## Accuracy Tests

**Needle-in-haystack retrieval:**
- T3 (4k context): ✅ PASS — correctly found "magic number 42" and "secret code BANANA"

items.title: [JIT] Fuse FP8 KV-cache quantization into the store kernel
items.body:
## Motivation

Fixes #30815.

With `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3`, `MHATokenToKVPool.set_kv_buffer` quantizes K/V eagerly before the store: in-place `div_` on k and v, two dtype casts, then the byte store. That is 5 kernel launches per layer per decode step with checkpoint KV scales (3 without), where bf16 KV takes a single fused JIT store. Measured on main 67e7f8d1 (RTX PRO 6000, SM120, CUDA 13, bs=1 decode, 8 kv-heads x 128, idle GPU):

| KV path | kernels / layer / step | latency (eager, min-of-medians) |
|---|---|---|
| bf16 | 1 | 22.4 us |
| fp8_e4m3 + scales, current | 5 | 57.2 us |
| fp8_e4m3 + scales, this PR | 1 | 30.7 us |

## Modifications

- `store_cache_quant` in `kernels/jit/csrc/elementwise/kvcache.cuh`: fused scale + FP8 cast + scatter store, one warp per row, vectorized 16B loads. Conversion follows the `per_tensor_quant_fp8` convention: fp32 multiply by the reciprocal, clip to the finite range, RNE convert (the eager `.to(fp8)` overflows to NaN instead of saturating). CUDA-only — on ROCm `fp8_e4m3_t` is a plain byte type, so HIP keeps the unfused path.
- Scales are accepted in the two forms callers actually pass: a 1-element float32 GPU tensor (`layer.k_scale`, read on device, no host sync) or a host float (`layer.k_scale_float`, reciprocal precomputed host-side).
- `set_kv_buffer` routes the fp8_e4m3 NHD CUDA path through the fused kernel; hnd/page-major/vectorized_5d layouts, dcp masks, e5m2, non-vector-multiple rows, and unsupported scale forms all keep the existing unfused fallback. Unlike the eager path, the fused kernel does not mutate `cache_k`/`cache_v` (callers currently `.clone()` to defend against that mutation; those clones can be dropped in a follow-up once this is the only engaged path).
- Tests in `test/registered/kernels/ops/kvcache/test_store_cache.py` (bit-exact vs the fp32 reference across batch sizes, row dims including epilogue-tail rows, both scale forms, int32 indices, input non-mutation, out-of-range saturation, `can_use` negative cases) and a benchmark `bench_store_cache_quant.py` (fused vs the eager sequence).

`set_kv_buffer_prefix_valid` (the prefill commit path) has the same unfused sequence with a 2-D loc shape; left for a follow-up to keep this PR one kernel.

## Accuracy Tests

- Unit tests: fused output is bit-exact against the fp32 reference (`clamp(x.float() * inv_scale, +-448).to(fp8)`) for all tested shapes and scale forms; 453 focused tests plus 9 subtests pass across `test_store_cache.py` and `test_asymmetric_mha_pool.py` on current main.
- Alignment safety: misaligned source bases or row strides take the eager fallback; the direct op rejects before launch, and a contiguous canary remains fused.
- Pool-level A/B through `set_kv_buffer` (stock vs fused, identical inputs): max difference is 1 fp8 code ulp on ~2% of elements — expected, the eager path rounds twice (bf16 divide, then convert) while the fused kernel rounds once in fp32, so the fused result is the more accurate of the two.

Current-main rebuild: based directly on `77c90e7e54938f9835c8d27563183f1ca2def4a6` as `9fc7b60e25bd91cb18d399cd05e8316452e9680a`; fresh outcome verification is `CONFIRMED`. The performance measurements below were not rerun and remain historical from the original implementation.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Kernel benchmark (`bench_store_cache_quant.py`, CUDA-graph timing, bf16 -> fp8_e4m3 with tensor scales, row 1024): fused 5.4 us vs eager 10.8 us at bs=1, 5.4 vs 13.5 at bs=16, 12.5 vs 44.0 at bs=4096 — 2.0-3.5x.

End-to-end `bench_one_batch`, Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct, bs=1, `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3`, interleaved stock/fused runs on an idle GPU:

- Eager decode (`--disable-cuda-graph`): median decode latency 7.95-8.36 ms stock vs 7.30-7.59 ms fused; fused faster in all three interleaved pairs (~8-11%), consistent with 26.5 us/layer x 28 layers.
- CUDA-graph decode: torch traces show the fused kernel engaged (28 `store_kvcache_quant` per step) and the KV-store kernel cluster down from 109.9 us to 44.7 us per 8 steps (2.46x); the whole-step effect at bs=1 on this small model (~0.3% of step GPU time) is below end-to-end run noise, so I am not claiming an end-to-end graph-mode win here. The launch-bound eager numbers above are where the reported ITL regression comes from.

## Checklist

- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).

items.title: [AMD] Quantize Q to FP8 in aiter decode unified_attention when KV cache is FP8
items.body:
## Motivation

On the AITER attention backend, the **extend/prefill** path already quantizes the query to FP8 and passes a `q_descale` when the KV cache is FP8 (`kv_cache_dtype == fp8_e4m3`), engaging the FP8 query-key kernel variant. The **decode** path in `forward_decode`'s `unified_attention` branch, however, left the query in bf16 and passed `q_descale=None`, so it dispatched to the `IS_Q_FP8_0` kernel variant even when the KV cache was FP8.

This PR makes decode consistent with extend: when the KV cache is FP8, the query is cast to FP8 and `q_descale` is supplied, so decode uses the same `IS_Q_FP8_1_IS_KV_FP8_1` unified-attention kernel as the FP8 KV path intends. This is also a prerequisite for checkpoints that carry real per-tensor Q/K FP8 scales (e.g. AttnFP8-quantized checkpoints), where the FP8 query path improves both attention throughput and numerics.

## Modifications

- `python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/aiter_backend.py`, `AiterAttnBackend.forward_decode`, `use_triton_unified_attention` branch:
  - When `self.kv_cache_dtype == fp8_dtype`, cast `q = q.to(fp8_dtype)` and set `q_descale = layer.k_scale if layer.k_scale is not None else self.k_scale`.
  - Pass `q_descale=q_descale` to `unified_attention(...)` instead of the previous hard-coded `q_descale=None`.
- No change to the bf16 KV path (when `kv_cache_dtype != fp8_dtype`, `q_descale` stays `None` and Q remains bf16).

Trace-confirmed kernel dispatch (Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-MXFP4, TP2, MI355, decode `CudaGraphReplay`):

| KV cache dtype | decode attention kernel variant |
|---|---|
| bf16 (unchanged) | `kernel_unified_attention_3d_..._IS_Q_FP8_0_IS_KV_FP8_0` |
| fp8 (this PR) | `kernel_unified_attention_3d_..._IS_Q_FP8_1_IS_KV_FP8_1` |

The FP8 path additionally issues a small `float8_copy` kernel to quantize Q (~4.8 µs/iter at conc64, summed over 15 attention layers).

## Accuracy Tests

GSM8K, 5-shot, 200 questions, same server config, bf16 KV vs FP8 KV (this PR active on the FP8 server). Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-MXFP4, TP2, MI355.

| Config | Accuracy | Invalid |
|---|---|---|
| bf16 KV (baseline) | 0.945 | 0.005 |
| fp8 KV (this PR) | 0.930 | 0.000 |

The Qwen3.5-MXFP4 checkpoint ships no k/v scales, so FP8 KV runs with scale = 1.0 (server logs the expected warning); the ~1.5-pt drop is attributable to scale-1.0 FP8 KV, not to the Q-FP8 change specifically. On checkpoints with real Q/K FP8 scales the FP8 query path is accuracy-neutral-to-positive.

## Benchmarking and Profiling

**End-to-end** (random, ISL 8192 / OSL 1024, range-ratio 0.8, ignore-eos, request-rate inf; num_prompts = concurrency × 10). Δ = FP8 KV (this PR) vs bf16 KV.

| Concurrency | total tok/s bf16 | total tok/s fp8 | Δ throughput | Median TPOT bf16 (ms) | Median TPOT fp8 (ms) |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 4 | 3,445.6 | 3,349.0 | −2.81% | 10.2 | 10.4 |
| 8 | 5,475.4 | 5,418.5 | −1.04% | 12.6 | 12.7 |
| 16 | 7,709.6 | 7,653.8 | −0.72% | 17.9 | 18.1 |
| 32 | 10,206.2 | 10,355.2 | +1.46% | 27.3 | 27.3 |
| 64 | 13,253.4 | 13,119.8 | −1.01% | 43.0 | 43.0 |
| 128 | 16,384.5 | 16,481.8 | +0.59% | 69.8 | 69.4 |

**Decode attention kernel** (profiling, num_prompts = concurrency × 2; per decode iteration, summed over 15 attention layers, TP-0). This isolates the kernel the PR engages:

| Concurrency | `unified_attention` bf16 (`IS_Q_FP8_0`, TILE16) | `unified_attention` fp8 (`IS_Q_FP8_1`, TILE32) | Δ | Q→fp8 `float8_copy` (fp8 only) |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 4 | 11.6 µs/call | 12.8 µs/call | +9.8% | +4.3 µs/call |
| 64 | 100.8 µs/call | 84.7 µs/call | −16.0% | +4.8 µs/call |

At high concurrency the FP8 KV/Q attention kernel is meaningfully faster (−16% at conc64, KV-read-bandwidth bound); at low concurrency it is slightly slower (batch too small to be bandwidth-bound, plus the added Q-quant). On this MoE model decode is MoE-bound (attention is ~7–11% of the decode iteration), so the net end-to-end effect is within run-to-run noise (±3%).

Note on scope: this A/B compares **FP8 KV (with this PR) vs bf16 KV**, not FP8-KV-with-Q-FP8 vs FP8-KV-without. The kernel table above is the direct, trace-confirmed effect of this change (the `IS_Q_FP8_0 → IS_Q_FP8_1` dispatch and the added `float8_copy`); the end-to-end table is provided for context.

items.title: [Fix] PureSWARadixCache: do not re-cache window-evicted KV (stale-KV read + double-free)
items.body:
## Motivation

On an all-SWA model whose attention backend is not prefill-aware, `req.swa_evict_floor` stays `0`, so `PureSWARadixCache.cache_finished_req` sets `insert_end = keys_len` and inserts the whole prefix `[0, keys_len)` into the radix tree.

But decode already freed the out-of-window range `[cache_protected_len, swa_evicted_seqlen)` via `free_swa_out_of_window_slots`, and `PureSWATokenToKVPoolAllocator` is single-pool (`full_attn_allocator is swa_attn_allocator`), so those slots are back in the free list. Re-inserting them means:

- `match_prefix` returns them as a cache hit, but the allocator has already recycled them to other requests, giving stale KV / wrong output;
- when the node is later evicted, `evict()` frees the same slots a second time (double-free of the pool).

The deterministic-mode (`is_insert=False`) branch has the same root cause and additionally double-frees the still-in-window tail within the same call.

This is reachable for any all-SWA model (`full_tokens_per_layer == 0`, selected in `registry.py`) with `prefill_aware_swa` disabled (the default) on any request longer than its sliding window.

## Modifications

Mirror decode's protection boundary. When a freed hole exists (`swa_evicted_seqlen > cache_protected_len`), only `[0, cache_protected_len)` is a live, contiguous prefix, so cache no further; the still-in-window tail is freed back to the allocator as before. When nothing was window-evicted the whole prefix is still cached, so short requests are unaffected, and the prefill-aware (`swa_evict_floor > 0`) path is unchanged.

## Tests

`test_pure_swa_radix_refree.py` (real tree/allocator/pool + mock Req, mirroring `test_swa_eviction_boundary.py`):
- after decode window-eviction, the freed prefix is not re-inserted and no slot is both allocator-free and tree-held (conservation);
- the `is_insert=False` path frees every slot exactly once;
- a short request (never leaves the window) still caches its full prefix.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Code Formatting with Pre-Commit](https://docs.sglang.ai/references/contribution_guide.html#code-formatting-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests as outlined in the [Running Unit Tests](https://docs.sglang.ai/references/contribution_guide.html#running-unit-tests-adding-to-ci).

items.title: [Feat][GLM5.2] Shared KV Cache for Prefill CP
items.body:
## Motivation DSA Prefill context parallelism requires every CP rank to consume the complete Main KV and Indexer history. Upstream main supports a layer-sharded path through [#29421](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/29421), using NCCL and remaining applicable across NVLink domains. This PR adds another option for same-host deployments within one peer-accessible NVLink domain: CP ranks share one CUDA VMM view and directly read peer-owned HBM pages. The two paths cover different topology and communication trade-offs. Like layer sharding, the shared layout stores one aggregate Main-K/Indexer cache instead of eight replicated copies, providing up to 8x logical cache capacity over Base CP8 for the same KV memory budget. The difference is the access model: instead of materializing each owner layer on every rank through a collective, attention kernels directly read peer-owned pages through the shared VMM view. On full GLM-5.2-FP8 / H20-3e, Shared KV stays within 1.86% of Base CP8 warmed mean Prefill latency through 256K. Base CP8 fits about 380K tokens in the tested configuration; Shared KV is intentionally capped at 1.2M tokens for the benchmark and successfully serves a 1M input. The tested 100K L2 host-cache restore reduces latency by 92.67%. ## Modifications - Add `--enable-dsa-shared-kv-cache` for same-host DSA L1/L2 sharing. - Store Main KV and Indexer once per CP group with owner-sharded CUDA VMM pages; kernels read the group-wide cache directly without per-layer KV broadcast. - Preserve the same ownership in page-first HiCache and Mooncake Prefill transfer, with mandatory CP synchronization before peer data is consumed. ## Design Logical page `p` is owned by CP rank `p % cp_size`, and each rank allocates only its owner pages. CUDA VMM exposes the physical allocations as one group-wide tensor view. Main KV uses the canonical view; Indexer adds a rank-local alias over the same physical allocation for the paged DeepGEMM path, without duplicating HBM. A mandatory CP write fence runs before any rank reads peer-owned pages. Page-first L2 keeps the same logical IDs and ownership. Each rank allocates pinned DRAM only for its owner pages and transfers only between local DRAM and local HBM. CPU failure agreement and a device fence complete each group-wide backup or restore. Mooncake Prefill transfer uses bounded registered staging buffers rather than a second HBM cache. The current scope is one host, one peer-accessible NVLink domain, GLM-5.2 DSA, FP8 KV, `tp=attn_cp`, interleaved Prefill CP, `pp=1`, page-first L1/L2, and Mooncake Prefill transfer. HiSparse, speculative decoding, and L3 storage are not enabled with this path. ## Trade-offs Both shared KV and layer sharding remove CP cache replication. They differ in how each rank accesses the complete cache: **Layer sharding** ```mermaid flowchart LR L1["Layers are sharded across CP ranks"] L2["Owner rank provides the current layer KV"] L3["Per-layer NCCL collective"] L4["Materialize full-layer receive scratch
on every CP rank"] L5["Attention reads local HBM"] LC["General NCCL-connected topology
Cost: transfer, collective sync, full-layer scratch"] L1 --> L2 --> L3 --> L4 --> L5 --> LC ``` **Shared KV (this PR)** ```mermaid flowchart LR S1["Logical page p → owner rank p mod CP size"] S2["Owner-sharded HBM mapped into
one group-wide CUDA VMM view"] S3["Owner-only page write"] S4["Mandatory CP publication fence"] S5["Attention directly reads
local or peer-owned pages"] SC["One peer-accessible NVLink domain
No per-layer KV collective or full-layer scratch"] S1 --> S2 --> S3 --> S4 --> S5 --> SC ``` | | Layer sharding | Shared KV | | --- | --- | --- | | Data access | Materialize the owner layer, then read local HBM | Read peer-owned pages through one VMM address space | | Communication | Per-layer collective transfer | No per-layer KV collective; mandatory write fence | | Temporary HBM | Full-layer receive scratch | No full-layer scratch | | Topology | Works across general NCCL-connected topologies | Requires one peer-accessible NVLink domain | | Main cost | Data movement and collective synchronization | Peer-HBM latency and write synchronization | In the current upstream implementation, the layer-sharded path has not yet optimized its communication to fetch only active/sparse KV. Under the matched setup used here, Shared KV reduces warmed mean Prefill latency by 49.01% at 4K (798.09 vs. 406.91 ms), 16.26% at 128K (14,877.29 vs. 12,457.69 ms), and 7.87% at 1M (179,701.77 vs. 165,565.18 ms). These results describe the current implementations rather than an inherent limit of layer sharding; the comparison should be repeated after its sparse-fetch communication path is optimized. ## Performance ### L1 Prefill Hardware/model: one H20-3e node, full 78-layer GLM-5.2-FP8, TP8/CP8, FP8 KV, `page_size=64`, `mem_fraction_static=0.88`, FlashMLA Sparse Prefill, FlashMLA KV Decode, and 8192-token chunks. Base CP8 disables cache sharding and supports about 380K tokens in this configuration. Shared KV uses `--max-total-tokens 1200000` as a test limit; this configured limit is not the architectural capacity ratio. Base CP8 uses `--cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 24` to fit its maximum capacity. All other workload and backend arguments match. **Metric:** mean end-to-end latency over three measured requests after one warmup request and a cache flush. This is a mean, not P90. With output length 1, E2E latency is used as Prefill latency. Actual concurrency is 0.995-1.000 and cache hit rate is 0% for every row. | Input | Base CP8 | Shared KV | Shared vs Base CP8 | | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | | 4K | 399.87 ms | 406.91 ms | +1.76% | | 32K | 2,891.98 ms | 2,913.81 ms | +0.75% | | 64K | 5,869.68 ms | 5,925.54 ms | +0.95% | | 128K | 12,331.04 ms | 12,457.69 ms | +1.03% | | 256K | 27,087.90 ms | 27,591.12 ms | +1.86% | | 512K | N/A (capacity) | 66,010.15 ms | N/A | | 1M | N/A (capacity) | 165,565.18 ms | N/A | The 4K-to-256K rows are matched performance comparisons. The 512K and 1M rows demonstrate the additional capacity and are not Base CP8 latency comparisons.
Server and benchmark commands ```bash SGLANG_JIT_DEEPGEMM_PRECOMPILE=0 \ PYTHONPATH=$PWD/python:$PWD/sgl-kernel/python \ python3 -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path /home/models/GLM-5.2-FP8 \ --tokenizer-path /home/models/GLM-5.2-FP8 \ --trust-remote-code \ --host 0.0.0.0 --port 30080 \ --tp-size 8 --attn-cp-size 8 \ --attention-backend dsa \ --dsa-prefill-backend flashmla_sparse \ --dsa-decode-backend flashmla_kv \ --enable-prefill-cp --cp-strategy interleave \ --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 \ --page-size 64 --mem-fraction-static 0.88 \ --max-total-tokens 1200000 \ --chunked-prefill-size 8192 \ --skip-server-warmup \ --enable-dsa-shared-kv-cache python3 -m sglang.benchmark.serving \ --backend sglang --host 127.0.0.1 --port 30080 \ --dataset-name random-ids \ --model /home/models/GLM-5.2-FP8 \ --tokenizer /home/models/GLM-5.2-FP8 \ --num-prompts 3 --max-concurrency 1 \ --random-input-len ${INPUT_LEN} --random-output-len 1 \ --random-range-ratio 1.0 --request-rate inf \ --tokenize-prompt --warmup-requests 1 --flush-cache \ --cache-report --output-details --disable-tqdm \ --seed ${SEED} --output-file ${OUTPUT_FILE} ```
### L2 HiCache With a 150K-token L1, `hicache_ratio=10`, page-first layout, `write_through`, kernel IO, and no L3, each rank allocates 11.57 GB for its owner pages. CP8 provides one aggregate 92.56 GB / 23,528-page L2 cache instead of eight replicated logical copies. An A/B1/B2/A test uses three distinct 100K prompts so B1 and B2 evict A from L1. Restoring A reports `device=0, host=99968`, reproduces `Paris` / token `[12089]`, and reduces E2E latency from 10,509.29 ms to 770.31 ms (-92.67%). No L3 backend is configured or observed. ## Correctness - Fixed short, 100K, and 128K output-1 prompts match Base CP8; a short semantic decode also matches. - GSM8K500 24-shot completion scores `0.956` against the registered `0.94` threshold. MMLU64 sanity scores `0.796875`, equal to ordinary Base. - Targeted CPU tests pass `90` cases, CP8 multi-GPU tests pass `3` cases, and the L2 host-only restore reproduces the cold answer. All changed-file pre-commit hooks and `git diff --check` pass.
